content:
Honest, my home-made iPhone camera mod looks pretty silly, but it actually makes iPhone photography more practical and a lot more fun.

What started as a solution for a single shoot gradually turned into a tool I instinctively reach for…

In the world of compact cameras, one of the longest-running debates has always been whether you really need a viewfinder. Traditional camera enthusiasts used to argue endlessly over whether electronic viewfinders (EVFs) or optical viewfinders were better, but EVFs have now become so good that almost nobody cares about it anymore.

Whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder does offer practical advantages over composing shots on the rear screen—especially under harsh sunlight. Even at maximum brightness, it is very hard to see the image clearly under a blazing sun, and the screen reflects light far too easily.

This is not normally a major issue in London, but this summer we experienced record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly I feel it has been roughly thirty years since I last saw a cloud or any rain.

But for me, the issue does not stop there. I have noticed a difference in visual immersion between using a viewfinder and using the rear screen—with a viewfinder you only see the image itself, but with the rear screen you also see the surroundings around you. Sometimes it is precisely that sense of immersion that makes me prefer to pick up a dedicated camera rather than the iPhone.

When I was choosing a video camera a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K (BMPCC 4K) was without doubt the most attractive option, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off. In the end I decided this was not a deal-breaker, because I mostly shoot indoors, and even outdoors, adding a large monitor with a sun hood solved most of the problems.

Still, sometimes I want something simpler to operate and do not want to lug around a whole rig with an extra monitor every day, so I found a simple accessory that is perfect for outdoor use. It is essentially a combination of a sun hood and a magnifier that attaches magnetically to the rear screen, giving you an experience similar to an optical viewfinder.

Recently I had a shoot that required using both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max at the same time. I went on location and did a quick test, and that viewfinder accessory was a huge help. Because the screens of the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone are similar in size, I wondered whether this accessory would also work on my iPhone.

The iPhone obviously does not have a magnetic array, but the phone is light enough that simply holding it up against the magnifier works perfectly. The effect surprised me—especially the fact that the Camera Control button can be used as a shutter release.

Since then I have been using this accessory in all kinds of situations, and being able to see the screen clearly under harsh sunlight, together with that sense of immersion, makes the whole process a lot more enjoyable. My iPhone has long been my main camera, and since fitting this DIY mod I have found myself reaching for the phone directly in more situations.

Genius or madness? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments. If you are on the pro side, I should mention that the model I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I have never seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, remember to drop the link in the comments.
